reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes an online earning opportunity through claims of earning 8,000 to 10,000 per month, and even 10,000 per day, by following the speaker's recommended methods on a mobile phone. The title and repeated "Live withdrawal" presentation use a displayed BUSD transfer and crowd footage as apparent proof to encourage participation in the promoted Forsage opportunity.

citations.quote: If you want to earn 10k per day you will just need to use your mobile
Listen closely to the methods I recommend you to follow and you will earn 8k, 9k , 10k per month
Live Withdrawal Online Work with Proof #Forsage BUSD Online Work

opening.argument: The presentation can be read as a personal demonstration accompanied by limitations, rather than a guarantee. The narration distinguishes between using a mobile phone and the speaker's recommended methods, while also saying the activity “didn't cost any money.” The wallet screen includes an explicit recipient-and-network warning before confirmation, underscoring that the transaction requires user review and carries operational risk. A displayed balance and transfer therefore show what one transaction looked like, not a promise that every viewer will earn a particular amount.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The earning figures are narration, but they do not by themselves establish a deceptive solicitation or a guaranteed outcome. “Live withdrawal” describes the demonstrated transaction, while the visible confirmation warning shows that the viewer must check the recipient and network. The prosecution's interpretation treats a balance display and crowd footage as proof of a scam without establishing what viewers were asked to pay or what result was guaranteed.

citations.quote: Live Withdrawal Online Work with Proof #Forsage BUSD Online Work

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The qualification about cost does not neutralize the unusually specific income claims. The narration still tells viewers they can earn “8k, 9k, 10k per month” by following recommended methods, and the transaction display is presented under “Live withdrawal.” A wallet warning concerns sending tokens safely; it does not warn viewers that the earning opportunity itself may be unreliable.

opening.argument: The strongest reading is an operational demonstration of a mobile wallet transaction and an online-work process. The sampled sequence shows a BUSD balance, a token page, an entered amount, and a transfer confirmation screen, while the narration tells viewers to listen to methods the speaker recommends. That is consistent with explaining how the process works or documenting personal use. The materials do not identify a promised enrollment result, a required payment, or a specific outcome for the audience; a demonstration should not be converted into a scam finding merely because it discusses possible earnings.

citations.quote: Listen closely to the methods I recommend you

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference argument assumes that discussing earnings makes the video a solicitation, but the supplied evidence also depicts concrete wallet operations. The title's word “Proof” can refer to showing a transaction, not certifying universal profitability. Neither the displayed transfer nor the narration establishes that viewers were required to join, deposit funds, or recruit others.

citations.quote: Live Withdrawal Online Work with Proof #Forsage BUSD Online Work

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling this a demonstration does not explain why the narration gives direct income amounts and instructs viewers to follow the speaker's methods. The wallet sequence supplies promotional-looking evidence for the earnings pitch: the title calls it “Online Work with Proof,” and the repeated overlay says “Live withdrawal.” Showing a transaction does not establish that the opportunity is educational or that the claims are reliable.

Online Work with Proof #Forsage BUSD Online Work

opening.argument: Even accepting that the video promotes an online service or work opportunity, the evidence does not establish a scam mechanism. The narration says the described activity did not cost money, and the visual sequence shows an ordinary BUSD wallet operation: a balance, a selected amount, and a transfer confirmation. There is no supplied evidence of a required deposit, a guaranteed return contract, credential collection, or downline-based income. A transfer to a wallet and a claim of online work may warrant independent research, but they do not by themselves prove deceptive acquisition of money or assets.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side identifies easy-income language, but it does not fill the missing mechanism. “10k per day” is a claim about potential earnings, not proof that viewers were asked to pay. The displayed BUSD transfer shows a transaction, while the supplied materials do not show a deposit demand, access fee, credential request, or recruitment structure. The category should not be inferred solely from promotional tone.

citations.quote: If you want to earn 10k per day

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a visible deposit request does not make the promotion ordinary commerce. The video pairs “online work” with claims of earning 8,000 to 10,000 per month and labels a wallet transaction “Live withdrawal.” The statement that it did not cost money is not a warning about risk or a clarification of eligibility; it can make the low-barrier earnings pitch more persuasive. The shown transaction does not validate the underlying opportunity.
